texts.facts: However, in terms of Section 52 of Food Safety and Page No.# 3/5 Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as Act, 2006), the punishment prescribed is now only fine upto Rs. 3 lakhs and therefore he submits that the petitioners should also get benefit of the aforesaid principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court. The learned counsel, however, has confined his argument to the sentence only. 4. To consider the aforesaid submission, this Court is to go through the complaint filed against the petitioners. The basic allegation in the complaint is to the effect that as per the Public Analyst Report, the turmeric powder and beson which is manufactured and sold by the petitioners are adulterated and mixed with rice powder. Such materials were seized from the possession of the petitioners. Accordingly, two petitioners were prosecuted.
texts.arguments: 6. Section 7 of the Act, 1954 prohibits any person to manufacture for sale or store, sell or to distribute any adulterated food and any misbranded food etc. 7. 8. The Act, 2006 was enacted with an object to consolidate the laws relating to food and to establish the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India for laying down science based standards for articles of food and to regulate their manufacture, storage, distribution, sale and import, to ensure Page No.# 4/5 availability of safe and wholesome food for human consumption and for matters Page No.# 1/5 vs The State Of Assam on 16 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99405015/ 2 connected therewith or incidental thereto. 9. Clause-(ii) of Sub Section 1 of Section 97 of the Act, 2006 on the other hand prescribes that such repeal shall not affect any right, privilege application or liability acquired, accrued or incurred under any of the enactment or orders under repeal. However, the Hon'ble Apex Court in Trilok Chand -Vs- State of Himachal Pradesh reported in 2020 10 SCC 763 referring to the earlier judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in T. Barai -Vs- Henry Ah Hoe reported in (1983) 1 SCC 177, more particularly relying on paragraph 22 of the said judgment, concluded that since the amendment was beneficial to the accused person it could be applied with respect to the earlier cases as well as which are pending in the Court. 11. In view of the aforesaid principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, the learned counsel for the petitioners argues that now the sentence is required to be modified as per Section 52 of the Act, 2006. 12. Section 51 of the Act, 2006 prescribes that any person who, whether by himself or by any other person on his behalf manufactures for sale or stores or sells or distributes or imports any article of food for human consumption which is substandard, shall be liable to a penalty which may extend to five Page No.# 5/5 lakh rupees.
texts.petitioner_arguments: In view of the aforesaid principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, the learned counsel for the petitioners argues that now the sentence is required to be modified as per Section 52 of the Act, 2006.
